insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's protocol has confirmed $4.51M in cryptographically verified GMV across 83,856+ receipts — each one a deterministic purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM on probabilistic targeting, this represents a structurally different data class: proof of transaction, not prediction of behavior.

Grocery-supermarkets (1,406 receipts, ~$40.47 avg basket) and restaurants-dining (1,212 receipts, ~$31.55 avg basket) together account for 52.3% of 14-day verified receipt volume, with gas-convenience and retail rounding out the top five — giving brand marketers a clean, receipt-verified category map of where wallet share is actually going.

insights.topic: Basket size stabilization after category mix shift
insights.insight: Average basket compressed from ~$48 to ~$40 as lower-ticket categories (coffee, dining) grew their share of receipt volume, but the compression appears to be plateauing — 7-day average basket ($42.34) is now running above the 14-day figure ($39.70), suggesting recent-day spend is holding or modestly firming within established categories.

insights.topic: Walmart structural dominance in verified purchase data
insights.insight: Walmart holds the top brand position across every observed 14-day snapshot at 368 receipts — 7.3% of all visible verified receipts — with Costco, Kroger, and Publix occupying the next three slots; together the top-5 brands account for 20.5% of 14-day volume, confirming mass-market grocery as the anchor of this verified purchase dataset.

The protocol is accumulating approximately 454 verified receipts per day, a rate that has held consistent across a 102-day observation window from ~37,576 to 83,856+ receipts; growth is decelerating but the deceleration rate itself is stabilizing, meaning the dataset is expanding at a predictable, investable pace rather than spiking or stalling.

insights.topic: Intraday purchase concentration — afternoon hours dominate
insights.insight: Receipt accumulation is consistently heaviest between 16:00–20:00 UTC, with the 2026-09-30 afternoon window alone adding 70 receipts and $3,232 in verified GMV in roughly 2.5 hours — a behavioral pattern that maps directly to end-of-workday shopping and has implications for daypart targeting and promotional timing decisions.
